sense: the character a person or thing is born with

terms.gloss: nature, character: what one is born with
evidence: Hor. Ep. 1.10.24: nātūram expellēs furcā, tamen ūsque recurret
Cic. Sen. 65: nōn omnis nātūra vetustāte coacēscit
terms.comment: By nature is nātūrā, in the ablative.

terms.gloss: a person’s nature, temperament; natural talent
evidence: Tac. Agr. 42.4: proprium hūmānī ingeniī est ōdisse quem laeserīs
terms.comment: Traupman’s word for a person’s nature. Lewis & Short call this general sense mostly poetic and post-Augustan, but Cicero uses it of a boy’s character, and it is everywhere a person’s talent.

terms.gloss: natural disposition, especially of the young
evidence: Cic. Sen. 26: adulēscentibus bonā indole praeditīs
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: an inborn or native quality; natural abilities, disposition.
One’s character as shown in conduct; indolēs is the inborn disposition.

evidence: Cic. Tusc. 5.47: quālis cujusque animī adfectus esset (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: A passing state of mind or feeling rather than inborn character.

phrases.latin: nātūram expellēs furcā, tamen ūsque recurret
phrases.english: you may drive nature out with a pitchfork, but she will keep coming back

phrases.latin: proprium hūmānī ingeniī est ōdisse quem laeserīs
phrases.english: it is human nature to hate the one you have hurt

phrases.latin: est magnum illud quidem vērum tamen multiplex puerī ingenium; quō ego regendō habeō negōtī satis
phrases.english: the boy has a great nature, but a complicated one, and steering it keeps me quite busy enough
